subject: Usage bands, overage terms, and temporary quota increases — follow-up
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@apexanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: usage bands, overage mechanics, and next steps

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying asks so we can get a scoped proposal over to Legal: 

Key signals from our discussion
- Expected steady-state tokens: 10M–25M / month (primary inference for features A/B)
- Peak patterns: short bursts tied to nightly job and enterprise demos; peak windows ~2–4 hours, up to ~2.5x sustained RPS versus baseline
- Target unit economics you mentioned: planning to land somewhere near $1,200–$1,800 per 1M tokens as a procurement target (we noted you want lower-end pricing if you can commit a floor)

Open questions we flagged on the call (asking you to confirm):
1) Floor vs ceiling: is Apex comfortable with an 8M token monthly committed floor and flexible ceiling (we’d price based on floor + tiered overage), or do you prefer no floor and a heavier overage discount if you cross X?
2) Burst windows: you asked whether temporary quota increases (for 2–4 hour windows) can be pre-authorized; please confirm the maximum single-burst multiplier you expect (example: 2x or 3x baseline) and frequency (once per month / ad hoc).
3) Billing cadence and overage grace: do you need overages to be netted against next-month credit (14-day grace) or billed immediately on the next invoice?

Here’s what I’ll do from Redwood based on the answers above:
- Draft three commercial options (consumption with soft cap, committed floor with tiered overage, reserved pool) and attach a draft rate grid so you can see unit economics at different bands.
- Include explicit temporary quota increase policy language and a sample operational runbook for approving short bursts.
- Put together a quick mutual action plan (attached: Apex-MAP-v1.pdf) and an internal rate grid (redwood-rate-grid-2026.csv).

Attachments: Apex-MAP-v1.pdf (proposal stub), redwood-rate-grid-2026.csv (unit econ examples)

Could you reply with answers to Q1–Q3 above by Thursday? If that works I’ll schedule a short legal handoff next week.

Thanks —
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@apexanalytics.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Legal Ops <legal@apexanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 16:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: usage bands, overage mechanics, and next steps

Sofia — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers: 

Q1) Committed floor: we’re comfortable with a minimum of 8M tokens/mo as a starting point if there is a clear breakpoint to renegotiate after two quarters. We’d like the ceiling to be flexible; billing should not auto-escalate to a higher committed tier without an explicit amendment.

Q2) Burst windows: typical bursts will be 2–3 hours, mostly around demos and batch scoring. We can tolerate a 2x multiplier on steady-state for routine bursts; for trade shows or conference demos we might need a one-off 3x. Ideally we want a pre-approved quick request path for 3x bursts but limited to 2 events per quarter.

Q3) Overage billing: we prefer an aggregated monthly billing approach with a 14-day reconciliation window (i.e., overage is invoiced on next invoice but not charged until reconciliation completes). If you have a mechanism to cap spikes that are flagged as accidental, that would be helpful.

Budget context: our procurement target is $15k–$20k/month for the first 3 months while we validate production performance. If the unit price is toward the $1,200/1M side we can scale faster.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, Apex Analytics
samir@apexanalytics.com | +1 206 555 0924

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: usage bands, overage mechanics, and next steps

Team — looping in proposed commercial options we can surface to Samir based on his answers. Draft language below (I also attached the rate grid used for internal math).

Option A — Consumption (no floor) with soft cap- Base unit price: $1,650 / 1M tokens (list)
- Soft cap threshold: customer can set soft cap; overages above soft cap are allowed but will trigger alerts and a 14-day grace recon before billing
- Overage charge: 1.25x list for the first 50% over soft cap, 1.5x thereafter
- Temporary quota increases: admin request path with auto-approval up to 2x sustained for up to 4 hours (max 2 events/quarter); ad hoc 3x requires SE approval

Option B — Committed floor (8M/mo) + tiered overage
- Floor price: $1,350 / 1M tokens applied to first 8M committed
- Overage tiers: 8–20M at $1,450 / 1M; 20–50M at $1,200 / 1M (volume discount kicks in)
- Billing: monthly; overages billed on next invoice with 14-day reconciliation window
- Temporary quota increases: pre-approved up to 2x for 3 hours; 3x events require written pre-approval from sales/legal

Option C — Reserved pool (Dedicated capacity)
- Committed pool with performance SLAs; unit price negotiable depending on GPU sizing (we can price after infra sizing call)
- Overages: additional reserved blocks billed at negotiated incremental price; emergency bursts handled by cross-region fallback at a premium

Operational notes:
- We can include a clause for a one-time onboarding allowance: first-month free buffer of 2M tokens to catch misconfigurations.
- We should materialize the temporary quota increase policy into the SOW with a maximum X-event rule and an approval log for audit.

Attachments referenced: redwood-rate-grid-2026.csv, Apex-MAP-v1.pdf

Ask: Sofia, recommend we present Options A+B initially; B maps to their stated procurement comfort (8M floor). Samir’s $15k–$20k/month band is roughly consistent with Option B near the midpoint if they land at ~12–15M tokens.

Ben Carter
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0199

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: usage bands, overage mechanics, and next steps

Samir — thanks for the quick replies and the budget context. Short summary and next steps: 

1) Proposal path: we’ll present Options A (consumption soft-cap) and B (8M committed floor) in a short proposal. Option B maps to your comfort with an 8M floor and gives clearer unit economics if you hit 12–15M.
2) Bursts: we’ll include operational language allowing auto-approved 2x bursts for routine windows and a documented request path for 3x events (limit 2 events/quarter).
3) Billing & overage: we’ll reflect the 14-day reconciliation window in both Options A and B; overage multipliers as Ben outlined.
4) Onboarding buffer: include a one-time 2M token onboarding allowance to catch misconfigurations.

Action items:
- Redwood (Ben/Sofia): finalize the two-option commercial draft and rate grid — target delivery: Friday EOD PT (attached draft).
- Apex (Samir/Legal Ops): confirm whether Legal needs a redlined SOW before the commercial draft; if yes, flag any must-have terms by Monday.
- Schedule: suggested 30-min handoff next Tuesday (May 26) to run Legal and Ops through the SOW and temporary-burst runbook.

If that looks right I’ll lock the calendar and send a DocuSign/Link to the SOW stub for review.

Cheers —
Sofia
